reward_shape_lineage:
Isaac-Asimov1-FallRecovery-v0 -- resumed from asimov1_fallrecovery_validated (iteration 15996, 89% unassisted success) across 4 further resumed runs this session, all chained (no fresh restarts), 21493 total iterations:
- Retrain #1 (15996->17495, +1500 iter): NO config changes, just continued training per the same pattern that originally took success_rate from 1% to 89%. Confirmed via the policy-stitching phase-machine demo: RECOVER->WALK handoff success rose 65.7%->69.2%.
- Retrain #2 (17495->19494, +2000 iter): also NO config changes. Handoff success rose further to 80.0% -- the best checkpoint before any reward-shape change (preserved as a fallback point).
- Retrain #3 (19494->21493 initial attempt, +2000 iter, SUPERSEDED/not used): added feet_slide (reused from the walking task) + a new RecoveryPositionDriftPenalty (anchors to root XY at episode start = where the robot fell, penalizes net drift past a 0.15m tolerance) at weights -0.25/-1.0, plus disabled the gravity-lift assist curriculum entirely (ASSIST_INITIAL_SCALE 1.0->0.0, confirmed no longer needed -- both recent retrains decayed it to 0.0 within a few hundred resumed iterations). Measured regression: handoff success FELL to 61.5% despite genuinely reducing the visible foot-sliding behavior -- a real example of a correctly-shaped single behavior change not translating to a better aggregate handoff rate. Rolled back to retrain #2's checkpoint rather than building on this one.
- Retrain #4 (resumed from retrain #2's 19494, +2000 iter, THIS CHECKPOINT): halved feet_slide/drift weights to -0.15/-0.4 (keep the direction, reduce how hard they compete against the primary height/pose objectives), and added a NEW recovery_pose_alignment_exp term (weight=2.0): an exp-kernel reward on joint-space L2 distance to WALKING_HANDOFF_TARGET_JOINT_POS -- the WALKING policy's own exact default/init pose, not just 'any valid standing pose' -- gated by height>0.9*STANDING_HEIGHT so it only applies once already near-standing. This directly targeted the hypothesis that good/bad handoffs were indistinguishable at the root-body level (confirmed via direct gate-value comparison across many handoffs) because the real gap was in the exact final JOINT configuration. Result: handoff success rose to 88.0% (22/25, best of the entire project), with the scooting/sliding also visibly reduced per live observation -- both the aggregate metric and the originally-targeted behavior improved together this time.
notes: Best validated fall-recovery checkpoint as of 2026-10-18. Policy-stitching handoff success progression across this session's retrains: 65.7% (baseline, asimov1_fallrecovery_validated) -> 69.2% -> 80.0% -> 61.5% (regression, not used) -> 88.0% (this checkpoint). Paired with asimov1_omni_robustness_validated (the walking checkpoint) for this measurement -- see that checkpoint's own notes for its side of the story. Gravity-lift assist is now a permanent no-op from iteration 0 of training (ASSIST_INITIAL_SCALE=0.0), confirmed unnecessary at this point in the lineage.
